rappel_detail.anchor: natural: slung horn, chockstone or gear; no fixed hardware
rappel_detail.station: The top of the damp, water-streaked dihedral where the descent ledges on the east side pinch out.
rappel_detail.notes: First of two near-full-length rappels on a single 60 m rope used doubled, down the dihedral.

rappel_detail.anchor: natural: slung horn, chockstone or gear
rappel_detail.station: Partway down the dihedral, at the end of the first rappel.
rappel_detail.notes: Second rappel, back to the top of the Overcoat Glacier. A shorter rope means more rappels.

set.rappel_count_note: Two rappels down the damp dihedral, each about as long as a single 60 m rope used doubled allows, are the commonly reported method; some parties downclimb the whole gully and ledge system when conditions allow. Anchors are natural, so carry cord and expect to leave gear. Exact lengths are not published.
